messages:
mira: Heads up — hit a weird silent hang in the Python SDK when using streaming (SSE / chunked). Happens after token refresh: client gets 401, refreshes, subsequent requests return 200 but the generator stops yielding and the socket remains open (no close, no final chunk).

sam: oof, can you paste a minimal repro + logs? which client version?

mira: repro attached (very trimmed):
```python
# simplified
client = RedwoodClient(token=short_lived_token)
resp = client.responses.stream(input='long prompt that triggers refresh')
for chunk in resp:
    print(chunk)
# after ~5m token expires -> 401 -> refresh flow
# afterwards generator prints nothing and never exits
```
logs:
```
2026-03-18T12:01:07Z INFO  401 token expired
2026-03-18T12:01:07Z DEBUG refresh ok
2026-03-18T12:01:08Z INFO  200 resumed connection
2026-03-18T12:01:08Z DEBUG no more chunks, socket open
```

sam: thanks. what's the exact package version + transport (requests/asyncio/httpx/uvicorn)?

mira: py-sdk 0.9.3, using async httpx on uvloop inside uvicorn dev server. Happens with both SSE and raw chunked on HTTP/1.1. Repro on mac + linux docker.

jia: does aclose()/aclose_stream() fix it if you call it from another task? or does that also hang?

mira: calling stream.aclose() from another task returns quickly, but the socket still shows ESTABLISHED (lsof/netstat) and server reports connection still open. So from SDK perspective it's closed but kernel socket not closed by peer.

sam: hypothesis: when auth refresh occurs we re-create auth headers and attempt to reuse the same connection. The server may send a half-close or not flush final chunk, and our generator coroutine awaits more chunks forever because the read loop expects either final chunk or connection EOF. If httpx/uvloop pools the connection and we put it back into pool incorrectly, that can silently drop chunk boundary events.

mira: sounds plausible. I also saw a rare case where final chunk was duplicated after refresh (two identical last chunks). Not always the same failure mode. :confused:

jia: can you try forcing connection close on refresh as a temporary workaround? e.g. set httpx limits to not reuse or call transport.close() before reauth. If that makes it go away, it's definitely connection reuse related.

mira: tried adding headers['connection']='close' on refresh — generator then properly raised GeneratorExit and socket closed. So definitely connection reuse related. Workaround is doable but sucks for perf.

sam: ok that's actionable. I'll draft a small fix: on receiving 401 during streaming, mark the streaming transport as 'drained/closed' and create a fresh transport for the post-refresh request. Also add a short watchdog that fails the generator if no chunks appear after N seconds post-refresh and surface a descriptive error.

jia: +1 on watchdog. Also add more explicit docs on how auth-refresh interacts with long-lived streams and recommended patterns (refresh tokens vs short-lived tokens and reconnect strategy).

mira: would love a small example in sample-apps showing how to do keepalive/reauth safely. This bit is a major onboarding friction for folks trying to use server-sent streams with short-lived creds.

sam: I'll open a PR: fix in transport + tests + an example app in examples/streaming/reactive-reauth.py. Will include an integration test that simulates 401 mid-stream and verifies the generator raises with a helpful message or reconnects appropriately when safe.

mira: awesome. can we also add a telemetry event so we can see how often this happens in the wild? (anonymous counts, not token info)

sam: yep — pinging ops: ci-bot to add a metric? @ci-bot

ci-bot: scheduled metric 'sdk.stream.reauth.hang' to telemetry queue (opt-in). :white_check_mark:

jia: assign to sam, but add me as reviewer. also add unit test for duplicated-final-chunk case (should dedupe or treat duplicate as final + close).

sam: will do. thanks for the quick triage. I'll link the PR here when it exists.

mira: thanks. leaving the minimal repro in a gist too: https://gist.github.com/mira/short-repro

sam: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-sdk/pull/412 (draft). includes workaround + perf note. requesting review from @jia.

jia: reviewing now. initial comments inline re: keeping the watchdog timeout configurable and not too aggressive.

mira: confirmed draft fixes my repro locally (fast but workable). Thanks all :heart:
